audit_findings.title: BASX growth may consume cash that owner earnings excludes
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 operating cash flow was $0.534 million versus $107.593 million of net income; accounts receivable, inventory, and contract assets absorbed $352.722 million gross, or $234.061 million after accounts-payable and contract-liability funding
audit_findings.mechanism: Required working-capital investment reduces distributable OE and makes the modeled growth rates require additional cash not deducted from the anchor or projections
audit_findings.evidence: Current payment terms for some BASX-branded jobs primarily require the Company to fund the upfront working capital resulting in cash outflows related to our contract assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash absorption is demonstrated and is large relative to the $113.0 million OE anchor. The record does not establish how much is temporary and recoverable versus a continuing investment required for BASX growth, but the observed scale is reasonably capable of materially reducing modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate normalized net operating working capital by BASX revenue cohort, collections cycle, and contract terms; deduct the non-recovering investment required under each growth scenario and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 interest does not represent the current debt run-rate
audit_findings.magnitude: Six-month 2026 interest expense of $11.250 million annualizes to $22.500 million, $4.774 million above FY2025; at the filed 25.0% normalized tax rate the difference is $3.581 million after tax, 3.2% of the $113.0 million anchor and approximately $0.45-$0.69 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher recurring interest charge lowers equity-level OE because the method retains interest expense rather than deducting debt principal in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had an outstanding balance of $398.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but its measured effect is small relative to both the valuation range of $14.07-$21.92 per share and the $79.40 market price. Correcting it would lower value but would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace FY2025 interest with annualized interest, commitment fees, and letter-of-credit fees based on the current debt perimeter, then confirm the resulting per-share values.

audit_findings.title: The anchor includes unusually favorable discrete tax benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: Applying the filed FY2025 normalized 22.5% rate to $128.752 million of pretax income produces a $28.969 million tax charge, $7.810 million above the filed $21.159 million charge; this is 6.9% of the $113.0 million anchor and approximately $0.97-$1.51 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Discrete tax benefits raise net income and therefore the OE anchor that is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Discrete events such as excess tax benefits related to stock compensation and various tax credits consistently provide a benefit, keeping our actual effective rate lower than the stated 22.5 %.
audit_findings.explanation: The favorable tax effect is demonstrated: FY2025 included $11.501 million of excess share-compensation tax benefits, and the normalized tax reconciliation indicates a $7.810 million anchor adjustment. Even that adjustment leaves every scenario far below the $79.40 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile sustainable credits separately from excess share-compensation benefits, normalize the anchor at the applicable recurring tax rate, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Required reinvestment may have been classified too aggressively as growth capex
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 property and software capital spending totaled $204.892 million versus the $113.0 million OE anchor, and the filed 2026 capital-expenditure program is approximately $190.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring capital spending omitted from maintenance capex overstates OE; reinvestment also constrains whether the modeled growth rates and terminal growth can be achieved
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital expenditure program for 2026 is estimated to be approximately $190.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish very large current investment, but they do not identify the amount required merely to maintain existing capacity, certifications, automation, software, and competitive position. Misclassification is therefore an unresolved possibility whose valuation materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every major capital and capitalized-software project to replacement, compliance, sustaining, or expansion purposes; rerun OE using the sustaining amount required for each growth scenario.

audit_findings.title: BASX earnings rely on estimates before final contract completion
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 BASX-branded revenue was $547.794 million, year-end estimated earnings on uncompleted contracts were $209.344 million, and June 2026 net contract assets were $246.121 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse cost-to-complete, penalty, acceptance, or settlement revisions would reduce reported earnings and the OE numerator; slower collections could also increase required working capital
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in job performance, job conditions, and estimated profitability, including those arising from contract penalty provisions and final contract settlements, may result in revisions to costs and income and are estimated and recognized by the Company throughout the life of the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: Reliance on estimated contract profitability is demonstrated and was identified as a critical audit matter, but no adverse revision or normalized error rate is supplied. The exposed balances are large relative to the $113.0 million anchor, yet the record cannot determine how much, if any, recognized profit is overstated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level estimate-at-completion roll-forwards, completion margins versus original estimates, penalties, loss provisions, acceptance status, and post-completion collections; adjust the anchor and rerun if systematic unfavorable revisions are found.

audit_findings.title: NMTC indemnities are contingent claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; recorded short-term and long-term NMTC obligations totaled $28.866 million at June 30, 2026, but that amount is not the disclosed maximum indemnity exposure
audit_findings.mechanism: A recapture payment would be a claim on equity value through the bridge or a cash charge to OE, separate from ordinary interest expense
audit_findings.evidence: Noncompliance with applicable requirements could result in the 2019 and/or 2023 and/or 2024 Investors' projected tax benefits not being realized and, therefore, require the Company to indemnify the 2019 Investor, 2023 Investor, and 2024 Investor for any loss or recapture of the 2019 NMTC, 2023 NMTC, and 2024 NMTC, respectively, related to the financing until such time as the recapture provisions have expired under the applicable statute of limitations.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnities are existing contractual contingencies, not demonstrated losses. The company states that it does not anticipate recapture, but the maximum exposure is undisclosed and the 2023, 2024, and new 2026 arrangements remain within seven-year compliance periods. The record therefore cannot establish valuation materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contractual maximum indemnity for each NMTC arrangement, compliance certificates, remaining recapture schedules, expiry dates, and any accrual or legal assessment; add probability-weighted or realized exposure to the bridge if supported.
